sources.entry: tern - Native SSH client written in Rust on GPUI, with saved hosts, a command picker, SFTP browser, split panes, port forwards and encrypted sync.

summary.one_liner: tern is a native macOS SSH client written in Rust on GPUI, with saved hosts, SFTP browsing, split panes, snippets, port forwards and Git-based encrypted sync.
summary.what_it_does: tern is a native SSH client for macOS, built in Rust on GPUI. It stores saved hosts with groups and tags, and imports them once from ~/.ssh/config. Terminal sessions support tabs, split panes, ⌘F search of the scrollback, snippets, and broadcasting input to chosen tabs. An SFTP browser lets you download files or drop files to upload. Connections support ProxyJump chains, local, remote and SOCKS forwards, agent forwarding, and two-factor logins. Passwords can come from your SSH key, a password-manager command, or an age-encrypted vault; ⌘\\ types a password only at a sudo-style prompt. Hosts, snippets and settings sync to a private Git repository, encrypted on the Mac before upload.
use_cases: manage many remote servers from one app
transfer files to and from a server over SFTP
keep SSH passwords out of plaintext using a password manager
sync SSH host lists across Macs via a private Git repo
set up port forwards or SOCKS proxies over SSH
run one command across several server tabs
how_to_run: Or download the signed and notarised DMG from the Releases page
notable: Passwords pulled from an external password-manager command, with ⌘\ typing them only at a password prompt
Sync encrypts data with age before it leaves the Mac; the Git repository only sees .age files and a metadata file
Checks host keys against ~/.ssh/known_hosts and refuses a changed key, showing the ssh-keygen -R fix
Automatic reconnect after network drops, but not after an explicit exit
Claims about 76 MB for one connected tab versus 580 MB for Tabby, measured by the author
caveats: Targets macOS; Windows and Linux builds are a preview that pass CI but have not been run on a real desktop yet
Per-host sync merges and password-command approval require manual steps on each Mac
